about:
# SquizzFrames

Party, raid, pet and unit frames for World of Warcraft Retail, built for patch 12.1.5.

Built around healing, where the frames are the game. Aura indicators run on Blizzard's own aura
system (AuraContainer), so they keep working in combat, when aura data is hidden from addons.

**[Download on CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1649203)** ·
[Changelog](https://github.com/SquizzCheeze/SquizzFrames/blob/main/CHANGELOG.txt)

---

## Features

**Party and raid frames**
- Separate party and raid layouts: size, spacing, position, growth direction (including centred)
  and opacity
- Raid frames laid out per group, with role sorting applied *within* each group
- Health colours by class, or by how hurt someone is (green through amber to red)
- Range fading, aggro, ready check, summon, drinking and phasing status, plus the game's ping
  markers on your frames
- Pet frames, attached to their owner or as a free group

**Indicators**
- HoTs can light up in gold during their refresh (pandemic) window, so you know when a recast
  won't waste time, in combat too
- Built-in indicators for HoTs, external and defensive cooldowns, debuffs (with a filter), crowd
  control, dispels (health-bar overlay and type icons), shields, heal absorbs, missing raid buffs,
  role, leader, raid marker, target and hover highlights, and more
- Custom indicators driven by your own spell lists
- Place any indicator anywhere with one anchor point and an offset, in a live preview
- One-click Healer preset

**Unit frames**
- Player, target, target of target, focus, focus target, boss and arena frames
- Arena frames show each opponent's spec, class and role before the gates open, and each
  enemy's trinket, crowd control and diminishing returns during the match (Blizzard's own icons,
  moved beside your frames)
- Cast bars, 2D/3D portraits, buff and debuff rows, absorb overlays, dispel overlays and icons,
  hover/target/aggro highlights, combat and leader icons, borders, and configurable text
- Attach unit frames and cast bars to Squizzumables' cooldown groups or Blizzard's Cooldown
  Manager rows, optionally matching their height

**Resource bar**
- A movable power bar plus your class resource points, together or placed separately
- Points as bars, shapes (round, star, heart, runes and more) or Blizzard's own class art, with
  rainbow colours and borders that follow the shape

**Party cooldowns**
- Your group's defensives, externals, group-wide and utility cooldowns as icons on their party
  frames, with countdowns, in combat and in Mythic+ (solo and party, not raids)
- Cooldown lengths follow each player's spec and talents; talents they didn't take are hidden
- Your own cooldowns exact from the game with charge counts; party members' two-charge spells
  show when a charge is left
- Everyone's combat potion, plus your own healing potion and Healthstone
- Below, above or beside the frame, in rows, with a per-spell on/off list and a live preview

**Tank tracker**
- A frame per tank showing their incoming debuffs above and their defensives below

**Click-casting**
- Bind spells, items, macros, target/focus and menus to any mouse button, key or mouse wheel,
  with any modifier
- Optionally extends the same bindings to Blizzard's player, target, focus and boss frames
- A heal aimed at a player who just died does nothing, instead of the game casting it on you

**Nicknames**
- Show a short nickname in place of a long character name: a private list only you see, plus an
  optional nickname shared with other SquizzFrames users in your group
- Your own entries always win, and incoming names are sanitised

**Everything else**
- Edit Mode alignment grid in your class colour, with snapping to the screen centre, edges and
  other frames, shared with Squizzumables
- Profiles that switch automatically by specialization and situation
- Hides the Blizzard frames it replaces, with one switch

## Installing

Install from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1649203), or
manually: download this repository and drop the `SquizzFrames` folder into

```
World of Warcraft\_retail_\Interface\AddOns\
```

Requires WoW Retail 12.1.5 (interface 120105). All libraries are bundled — there
is nothing else to install.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `/sf` | Open the options panel |
| `/sf lock` / `/sf unlock` | Lock or unlock the frames for dragging |
| `/sf healer` | Apply the healer preset |
| `/sf nick` | Nickname management (run alone for usage) |
| `/sf notes` | Show this version's release notes again |
| `/sfcdcheck` | Compare Party Cooldowns' lengths for your spells with your tooltips |
| `/sf reset` | Reset the profile and reload the UI |

`/squizz` is not used — that belongs to another addon.

## Bugs and requests

Please open an issue. A copy of the error text (BugSack or
similar) and what you were doing at the time is enormously helpful, especially
for anything that only happens in combat.

## Credits

Secure frame and indicator techniques were learned from **Cell**,
**DandersFrames** and **EllesmereUIRaidFrames**, and from Blizzard's own
FrameXML source. All code here is written for SquizzFrames.

Bundled libraries: Ace3, LibStub, CallbackHandler-1.0, LibSharedMedia-3.0,
LibCustomGlow-1.0, LibRangeCheck-3.0, LibDeflate, LibSerialize — each under its
own license — plus LibSquizzGrid-1.0, shared with Squizzumables.

## Support

If you enjoy using SquizzFrames, consider supporting development on
[Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/squizz) ❤️

## More addons by Squizz

- **[Squizzumables](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1483099)** — one-click reminders for food, flasks, oils and class buffs, plus raid tools and a restyled Cooldown Manager
- **[Squizzcap](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1713974)** — what killed you, how hard it hit and how fast you went down, with every death of a key saved to look back on
- **[SquizzTalents](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1705647)** — all your talent builds in one list, with a reminder when your build doesn't match the content
- **[DPS Report](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1504877)** — a lightweight damage meter with spell breakdowns and an end-of-key MVP summary
- **[Avatar Continued](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1533608)** — your character model on screen as part of your UI
- **[KSLBestDungeon](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1599575)** — ranks Mythic+ dungeons by how many of your KeystoneLoot favorites drop there

## License

[MIT](https://github.com/SquizzCheeze/SquizzFrames/blob/main/LICENSE).

SquizzFrames - Changelog
========================

V2.7 (2026-11-28)
-----

Fixed:

- Unit frames: text moved over the portrait with its offsets (the Level
  text, for example) now draws on top of the portrait instead of behind it,
  on the frames and in the options preview.

V2.6 (2026-11-28)
-----

New:

- Unit frames: the Level text can colour itself by difficulty, the way
  Blizzard's target frame does: grey, green, yellow, orange or red against
  your own level, for units you can attack. On by default (Difficulty Color,
  under Level); friendly units keep the text colour you picked.
- Options window: the sidebar scrolls when it has more rows than fit, and
  pages are built a few at a time instead of all at once on the first open.

Fixed:

- Click-casting: "script ran too long" in a full raid, most often on
  leaving combat. Re-applying bindings cleared every possible click-cast
  setting on every frame (about 400 each, 16,000 across a raid) in one go;
  our own frames now clear only the bindings actually written to them.
- WoW Forever: out-of-range fading could fail to start, because the range
  library tried to listen for an event Forever does not have and stopped
  there. It now only listens for events the game knows.

V2.5 (2026-11-21)
-----

New:

- Party and raid frames: a Level Text indicator (Indicators > Vitals), off by
  default. Shows the level, or level and class, in any colour or the class
  colour, and by default hides itself for anyone at max level, so while
  levelling it only shows who is behind. Works on retail and WoW Forever.
  The unit frames already had this: turn on the Level text on any frame.

Fixed:

- Resource bar: Druids get Combo Points in Cat Form whatever their
  specialization, the same rule Blizzard's own bar uses. Only Feral and
  Guardian got them before, so Balance and Restoration in Cat Form had none,
  and on WoW Forever no Druid did.

V2.4.1 (2026-11-18)
-----

Fixed:

- WoW Forever: the spell checklists on Healer HoTs and the other built-in
  indicators no longer spill over each other. A spell with more than three
  ranks shows the number of ranks, and hovering it lists every spell ID.

V2.4 (2026-11-17)
-----

New:

- Unit Frames > General > Blizzard's Frames: "Always Hide Blizzard's" Player,
  Target and Focus Frame. Hides Blizzard's frame even when SquizzFrames' own
  frame (or all unit frames) is switched off.

Fixed:

- A cast bar with its own position, or attached to another frame, now keeps
  working with its unit frame switched off. Before, turning the Player Frame
  off took the player cast bar with it. A cast bar set to sit on its frame
  still goes with the frame.
- Converting a party to a raid (or back) in combat now swaps to the right
  frames straight away. Before, a party kept its party-sized frames until
  combat ended, and a raid turned into a party showed no frames at all.
- A removed click-cast binding that used two or more modifiers kept working
  until a /reload.
- The right-click menu now follows combat correctly when you were already
  hovering a frame as combat started or ended.
- Mouse-wheel and keyboard click-cast bindings no longer stay stuck on a
  frame that disappears under the cursor (a member leaving, a party/raid
  swap), which could stop the wheel zooming the camera.
- Less work after loading screens and in busy fights: click-cast bindings
  are written once instead of three times after each loading screen, and the
  Drinking check, Missing Buffs, indicator updates and Party Cooldowns all do
  less per event. Party, raid, pet and unit frames, the indicators and the
  Tank Tracker now only hear health, power and aura updates for the units
  they show, instead of for every nameplate on screen.

V2.3 (2026-11-11)
-----

New:

- WoW Forever: your hunter pet's happiness shows as an icon on your pet's
  frame, and hovering the frame adds its mood, damage and loyalty to the
  tooltip. Size, anchor and offsets are under Pet Frames > Pet Happiness.
- WoW Forever: Name Text's "Hide Realm Name" is now labelled "Hide Surname",
  which is what it hides there. Surnames that are shown now use the game's
  own separator instead of a hyphen.

V2.2 (2026-11-05)
-----

New:

- Profiles can be shared as a string: Import / Export on the Profiles page.
  An import is always added as a new profile, so nothing you have is
  overwritten. Click-cast macros are removed unless you tick the box to keep
  them, so only keep them from someone you trust.
- WoW Forever: Party Cooldowns have their own spell list, with every rank of
  each spell, and hide spells a character is too low level to have.
- WoW Forever: HoT, external, defensive and missing-buff indicators and the
  click-casting spell list now use Forever's spells, every rank included.
  Smart Resurrection casts the right spell for your class. The Arena tab is
  gone there, since Forever has no arenas.
- WoW Forever: ping markers show on the party and raid frames, using Forever's
  own ping art.

Fixed:

- A member leaving, joining or being re-sorted during combat no longer
  leaves the party and raid frames showing the wrong people until the
  fight ends. Health, names, status, aura indicators and Party Cooldowns
  now follow the change straight away, in combat too.
- A member who joins during combat now gets a full frame straight away:
  health bar, the right size, and all indicators including HoTs, debuffs
  and dispels. Before, the frame stayed blank until the fight ended.

V2.1 (2026-10-27)
-----

New:

- Party Cooldowns (Tools > Party Cooldowns, off by default): each group
  member's defensives, externals, group-wide and utility cooldowns as
  icons on their party frame, with countdown numbers, a shade while on
  cooldown and a highlight while active. Works in combat and in Mythic+.
  Solo and party only, never in a raid.
- Cooldown lengths follow each player's spec and talents (yours directly,
  party members' after an out-of-combat inspect), and talent cooldowns a
  player did not take are hidden.
- Your own cooldowns are read exactly from the game, with a charge count.
  Party members' two-charge spells darken with a number only when no
  charge is left, and show a thin bar along the bottom while recharging.
- Potions: everyone's combat potion, plus your own healing potion and
  Healthstone.
- Place the icons below, above, left or right of the frame, aligned to
  either end or centred, in up to four rows, with offsets, size, spacing,
  shade and number size. Optional tooltips on hover, and a live preview on
  the options page that matches your frames' colours.
- Every spell can be switched on or off on its own (Spells tab, grouped by
  class, with All On / All Off).
- /sfcdcheck compares your own cooldown lengths with your tooltips.
- Cooldowns that leave no buff on anyone (interrupts, most damage
  cooldowns, other players' healing potions) cannot be seen in instances.

V2.0.1 (2026-10-18)
-----

Fixed:

- With Squizzumables, a resource bar or cast bar attached to a Cooldown
  Manager row (Blizzard's or Squizzumables') no longer loads in the wrong
  place and jumps into position a couple of seconds after login or /reload.

V2.0 (2026-10-17)
-----

- A member who joins during combat now gets a full frame straight away:
  health bar, the right size, and all indicators including HoTs, debuffs
  and dispels. Before, the frame stayed blank until the fight ended.

New:

- Party Cooldowns (Tools > Party Cooldowns, off by default): each group
  member's defensives, externals, group-wide and utility cooldowns as
  icons on their party frame, with countdown numbers, a shade while on
  cooldown and a highlight while active. Works in combat and in Mythic+.
  Solo and party only, never in a raid.
- Cooldown lengths follow each player's spec and talents (yours directly,
  party members' after an out-of-combat inspect), and talent cooldowns a

- Your own cooldowns are read exactly from the game, with a charge count.

  the options page that matches your frames' colours.
- Every spell can be switched on or off on its own (Spells tab, grouped by
  class, with All On / All Off).
- /sfcdcheck compares your own cooldown lengths with your tooltips.

  cooldowns, other players' healing potions) cannot be seen in instances.
